description: Rewrites the campaign's own texts around facts that already changed, and only the parts you picked: the copy on the registration page and the emails. Take it when a date or a name moved and several lines still carry the old facts. A host says: "The whole page still talks about March, make it fit the new date." It needs the session, the webinar and the parts to rewrite. Without a clear yes nothing is written; the answer is a preview of which parts would change, one line each, so the host can pick. With the yes the picked parts are rewritten and the rest stays exactly as it was. The thank-you page, the webinar name and the room info text are not written here; a single wording is better changed with wi_change_webinar_text. Side effect: it acts on your connected WordPress site; nothing else is touched. Words hosts use: rewrite the page, texts out of date, fix all the dates, refresh the copy

confirm.description: true actually rewrites the chosen parts. Leave it out to get the preview first and let the host pick.

primary_goal.description: What should be different for the participants afterwards, if that changed.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

target_audience.description: Who the webinar is for, if that changed.

targets.description: Which parts to rewrite: the registration page copy, the emails, or all of them. These are the only parts this tool can write.

topic.description: The topic, if it changed and the new copy should know it.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

name: wi_rewrite_webinar_texts
title: Rewrite the webinar texts after the facts changed
